title: Which group should count them?
hook: An offer is randomized; accepting it is not. Which comparison survives?

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: analyze by assignment or by who actually complied; only one stays unbiased.

misconception: Treating intent-to-treat vs per-protocol as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: analyze by assignment or by who actually complied; only one stays unbiased.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: In each randomized arm, 40% are willing types with baseline 3 and 60% have baseline 0. Only willing offered people take treatment, which adds 5. What is the assignment effect?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-intent-to-treat-vs-per-protocol/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Randomized assignment offer yes/no. In offer group4 take treatment(mean effect5),6 not; assignment effect2 across10. Per-protocol selected groups may differ baseline; show a baseline shift+3 creates naive per-protocol8.

claims.text: Assignment retains a difference of 2; the selected taker comparison retains 8. The takers combine a treatment gain of 5 with a baseline advantage of 3.

claims.text: Analyzing by randomized assignment preserves the randomized comparison and measures the offer’s effect. Comparing people who chose to comply changes the groups; it needs additional assumptions to recover a treatment effect.

claims.text: An offer reaches 25% of people and adds 8 for those reached, with no other effects. What is the assignment effect? The offer averages 0.25×8=2 across everyone assigned, under the stated uptake and exclusion assumptions.
